Hi Michael / Ava — following up on the measurement and exclusion questions with technical detail so legal has concrete language to work from. Key points below: 

- What we measure: by default our SLA measures server-side request accepted timestamp to final-byte-sent for non-streaming responses (model-inference + runtime overhead). For streaming, we provide two metrics: first-byte latency (time from server receive to first chunk delivered) and completion latency (time to final token). The SLA percentile (e.g., p95) will be applied to the relevant metric in the agreement (we can specify p95 on first-byte and p95 on completion separately if you prefer).

- Percentiles in SLA: we typically use p95 for customer-facing SLAs. p99 is available as a diagnostic metric but is not tied to financial remedies by default. If you want p99 in the SLA we can discuss tighter commitment and pricing implications.

- Exclusions (explicit): 
  - Scheduled maintenance windows (we recommend up to 4 hours/month; we will notify 72 hours in advance for planned maintenance).
  - Emergency maintenance necessary to mitigate production incidents or critical security patches.
  - Customer-caused issues: misconfiguration, customer-side network outage, API key misuse, or exceeding agreed rate limits.
  - DDoS/force majeure events.
  - Capacity exhaustion due to customer-initiated load testing outside of agreed test windows.

- Measurement method / sampling: Latency is measured at the load-balancer edge in our control plane to capture server-side end-to-end. We exclude client-side network variability. For determinism, we sample all production traffic for SLA calculations (no synthetic-only measurements).

- Remedies: Standard crediting model: 
  - < 99.9% monthly uptime / SLO achievement: 5% service credit
  - < 99.0%: 10% credit
  - < 95.0%: 25% credit and executive review
We can provide contract language examples and make credit tiers configurable per enterprise agreement.

- Reporting: monthly SLA report with p50/p95/p99 distributions plus on-demand raw export (CSV/JSON) via a secure link. We can also provide streaming-first-byte dashboards in the Console.

I'll attach a short appendix with definition snippets you can paste into the SLO clause. If helpful, we can include sample queries and the exact PromQL we use to derive percentiles.

Let me know if you'd like us to measure first-byte p95 as the primary SLA metric for streaming — that is straightforward to configure.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
